title: Add RAG step-handoff patterns and lightweight tool shims quickstart
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: New quickstart: step-handoff patterns + lightweight shims to standardize tool-calling boundaries in RAG orchestrations. Includes docs, runnable examples, and CI smoke tests.
commits: feat: add step-contract schema and example templates
feat: add lightweight http/kv shims and ts examples
chore: add CI smoke workflow and docs site nav entry; address linting feedback
body:
Summary: Introduces a compact quickstart that demonstrates a deterministic step-handoff pattern for RAG orchestrations and a set of small, lightweight tool shims (HTTP and KV) used during local development and CI smoke runs. Motivation: engineers frequently build RAG flows where the LLM decides to call external tools; we observed drift and brittle contracts between steps. This quickstart codifies a minimal contract (step-contract.yaml) and provides runnable shims to reduce friction when onboarding tool integrations and writing deterministic tests.

What changed (single-line description): added quickstart directory with templates, examples (TS), docs site page, CI smoke workflow, and lightweight shims to emulate common backend tools.

Why: Reduce iteration time when constructing tool-calling agents and increase reproducibility for evals/smoke tests. The step-contract schema helps teams define required input/outputs per step and enables lightweight validation in the orchestrator.

Key files: quickstarts/rag-step-handoff/README.md — quickstart instructions and local run steps; templates/step-contract.yaml — compact schema describing step boundaries and required fields; examples/*.ts — minimal agent runner and shims for HTTP and KV backends; docs/playbooks/rag-step-handoff.md — docs site guide and motivations; .github/workflows/rag-step-handoff-smoke.yml — CI job that boots the shims, runs the example agent, and validates a deterministic trace.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart README with step-by-step local run and troubleshooting - [x] Minimal step-contract schema + example contract - [x] Runnable TypeScript examples with tiny shim servers (no external infra) - [x] CI smoke workflow that runs headless and validates step outputs - [x] Docs site entry and sidebar link - [x] Linted and tested (fixes included)

Implementation notes and design decisions: - Step contract: intentionally small (name, inputs schema, outputs schema, required_assertions). The contract is YAML first to be human-editable in authoring workflows. Teams can adopt a stricter JSON Schema if desired. - Shims: two shims included: http-shim.ts (mocks an external HTTP tool with configurable behaviors) and kv-shim.ts (in-memory key-value store used to emulate retrieval or caching tools). Both expose a minimal HTTP API used by the sample agent-runner.ts so the developer experience is "shellless"—no need for Docker or cloud services to run examples. - Determinism: CI smoke job runs with a fixed prompt/seed and verifies the step outputs against assertions in step-contract.yaml. This reduces flakiness in docs examples and simplifies troubleshooting for first-time users. - Compatibility: examples use the Redwood SDK pattern present in quickstarts (simple fetch/SDK wrapper); we avoid depending on internal runtime code so the quickstart stays runnable for external community contributors.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged lint failures and a flaky timeout in the smoke job. Fixes applied: reduce timeouts in local shim startup, add explicit readiness probe, and run lint fixes across JS/TS files. Final CI: 1 workflow (smoke) passed, unit lint passed, integration smoke completed in ~45s using GitHub Actions hosted runner. CI logs are included in the PR checks.

Review notes and conversation summary: Marco: asked to tighten the step-contract example to include an explicit "error_handling" field. Author: updated templates and added examples showing how to annotate non-retriable errors. Jinsoo: requested an explicit example of the orchestrator skipping a step when contract assertions fail — added a small snippet in snippets/hand-off-flow.md and a unit test in examples/ts/step-handoff-client. Renee: requested clearer docs for how to plug in a real backend instead of the shim — added the docs section "Replacing shims with real backends" and sample env var mappings.

Backwards compatibility: Non-breaking. This is an additive quickstart and does not modify existing APIs.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash after approvals from Marco and Jinsoo. The PR closed when CI passed and docsite preview link verified the new page renders correctly.

How to try locally (short): 1) cd quickstarts/rag-step-handoff 2) npm install (in examples/ts/step-handoff-client) 3) npm run start:shims (starts http-shim and kv-shim) 4) npm run start:agent (runs agent-runner.ts against shims) 5) observe deterministic trace and assertion pass.

Related: ENG-7832 (implementation spike), PM-154 (docs initiative for quickstarts), and a follow-up task to convert the step-contract to a JSON Schema for validation tooling.
review_comments: Marco Diaz (reviewer): Can we add an explicit error_handling clause to the example contract? Some teams need non-retriable vs retriable semantics.
Aisha Patel (author): Good point — added error_handling and example annotations (see templates/step-contract.yaml).
Jinsoo Kim (reviewer): Please add an example of how the orchestrator will skip a step when contract assertions fail — it's a common pattern.
Aisha Patel (author): Added hand-off snippet and unit test under examples/ts/step-handoff-client to illustrate skipping logic.
Renee Carter (reviewer): Docs need a short section on how to wire the shims to real backends (env var mapping).
Aisha Patel (author): Added 'Replacing shims with real backends' in docs/playbooks/rag-step-handoff.md and updated README troubleshooting.
CI bot: Lint failed on first run (unused imports). Author pushed fixes and re-ran CI. All checks passed.
